summary: Iteration 6 (Iteration-10 features) full backend + frontend test. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iter6_permissions.py (27 tests) covering the permission-key registry, per-user grant/revoke overrides, RBAC on payouts/run-now + mark-paid + channel-partner create/patch, CAM templates CRUD/RBAC, and CAM PDF regression. Full suite: 111/111 pytest passing (run twice, no flakes). Playwright covered /channel-partners (KPIs, leaderboard, detail modal + 6-month sparkline, Release commissions -> confirm -> toast -> /payouts?batch=), /payouts?batch=<id> amber-ring highlight, the 3-step partner wizard end-to-end, CAM load/apply/save template dialogs, /admin/permissions manage modal, and permission-gated button hiding. 3 real defects found: phantom batch_id from run-now when nothing is eligible (breaks the one-click release flow on 2nd+ use), permission grants not usable end-to-end because the read endpoints still use hardcoded role checks, and GET /api/users + /admin/permissions page have no authorization gate.

critical.issue: When no eligible cp_commissions/incentives remain, server.py:1884 returns an early payload containing a FABRICATED batch_id (PO-2026-08-xxxxxx) that is never inserted into payout_batches. Reproduced: two consecutive calls returned PO-2026-08-b2416a and PO-2026-08-fd75ae while GET /api/payouts still lists only the one real batch PO-2026-08-61e129. Frontend then shows a success toast 'Batch PO-... prepared - Rs.0' and navigates to /payouts?batch=<phantom>, where no row exists so no amber highlight is applied. The toast.info('No eligible commissions to batch.') branch in ChannelPartners.jsx:196 is dead code because data.batch_id is always truthy. Return batch_id: null (or omit it) in the empty branch.

The new permission system only replaced the role checks on the MUTATION endpoints. These read endpoints still hardcode role lists, so an admin-selected user cannot actually use a granted permission. Verified: granted release_commissions+create_partner to a sales_agent -> POST /payouts/run-now = 200, but GET /partners/performance = 403 'Not allowed' (so /channel-partners page never renders and the Release button is unreachable) and GET /payouts = 403 'Finance only' (batch cannot be viewed). Requirement 'ONLY for admin or admin-selected users' is therefore broken for admin-selected users.

server.py:1391 only calls require_user() - no role/permission gate. Any authenticated principal can dump the full staff directory including emails and roles. Verified 200 with the channel_partner session token (test_session_partner). This is the datasource for the new /admin/permissions page, which itself is not gated either (see frontend issues). Gate with require_permission(user, 'manage_users') or a staff-role check.

ui_bugs.issue: Sidebar.jsx:53 renders the 'Permissions' nav link (nav-permissions) for every user and App.js:146 mounts /admin/permissions with no permission guard. A customer/channel_partner can open the page and read the whole user directory (GET /users is ungated). Only the per-user Manage modal correctly 403s. Gate the link + route on manage_users.

run-payout-btn and markpaid-<id> buttons are not permission-gated in the UI, unlike ChannelPartners.jsx which hides its buttons via perms.has(). Backend does enforce 403, so users without release_commissions/mark_payout_paid see enabled buttons that fail with an error toast. Inconsistent UX.
Same phantom-batch consequence as the backend issue: toast.success(`Batch ${data.batch_id} ready - Rs.0`) fires even when nothing was batched. Should branch on cp_count/incentive_count/total_amount.

No loading state - the table shows 'No users match.' while GET /users is in flight (captured in screenshot immediately after page load, 0 perm-row-* elements). Add a loading skeleton and distinguish empty-from-loading.

Permission-gated controls pop in 1-2s after first render because the hook starts with permissions: [] while /me/permissions resolves (cam-save-template-btn was absent immediately after the CAM tab rendered, then appeared). Consider a loading/disabled placeholder to avoid layout shift and false 'no permission' impressions.

integration_issues.issue: Works only on the first run of a period. Verified click -> window.confirm -> POST /payouts/run-now -> toast -> nav to /payouts?batch=PO-2026-08-ddd4f8, but that batch_id was a phantom so [data-testid=batch-row-PO-2026-08-ddd4f8] never existed and no highlight/scroll happened. With a real id (/payouts?batch=PO-2026-08-61e129) the amber ring works: class 'bg-amber-50 ring-2 ring-amber-300' + scrollIntoView.

action_items: server.py:1884 - do not return a fabricated batch_id when there is nothing to batch (return batch_id: null / omit), and make ChannelPartners.jsx:192 + Payouts.jsx:24 branch on it so the 'No eligible commissions to batch.' info toast actually fires instead of navigating to a non-existent batch.

Replace the remaining hardcoded role checks with has_permission on GET /api/partners/performance, GET /api/payouts and GET /api/payouts/{batch_id}/csv, otherwise a user granted release_commissions still cannot reach /channel-partners or /payouts.
Add authorization to GET /api/users (manage_users or staff-only) - it currently leaks the full user directory to channel_partner/customer sessions.
Gate the sidebar 'Permissions' link and the /admin/permissions route on the manage_users permission.
Permission-gate run-payout-btn and markpaid-<id> on the Payouts page for consistency with ChannelPartners.
Add a loading state to AdminPermissions (currently renders 'No users match.' while loading).
critical_code_review_comments: _process_payout_batch() generates batch_id before it knows whether anything is eligible and returns it on the empty path without persisting - any caller that trusts batch_id (both UI call sites) breaks. Generate the id only after the eligibility check.

Permission enforcement is split across two paradigms: require_permission/has_permission on mutations vs `if user['role'] not in (...)` on reads (payouts list, payouts CSV, partners/performance). This makes grants non-functional and is the root cause of backend issue #2.
GET /api/users returns the full users collection to any authenticated principal - no role filter, no field projection beyond _id. It is now reachable from a nav link visible to every role.
ChannelPartners.jsx is 466 lines with the page, PartnerDetail and PartnerWizard in one file; extracting PartnerWizard would keep it under control as more steps are added.

fetchMyPermissions() caches a module-level promise forever, so a permission change made by an admin is not reflected for the affected user until a full page reload; clearPermissionsCache() is exported but never called after AdminPermissions saves.

success_rate.backend: 100% (111/111 pytest; 3 defects are gaps not covered by asserts on the documented contract - documented above)
success_rate.frontend: 88% (release-commissions deep link broken on repeat runs; authorization gating gaps)

rca_of_the_issue: Phantom batch: _process_payout_batch() (server.py:1873) computes `batch_id = f"PO-{period}-{uuid4hex6}"` BEFORE querying eligible items, then the `if not cp and not inc:` guard at line 1883 returns that id with zero counts without inserting into payout_batches. Both UI callers treat a truthy batch_id as success - ChannelPartners.jsx:192 navigates to /payouts?batch=<id> and Payouts.jsx:24 toasts 'ready'. Because commissions are stamped with batch_id on the first successful run, every subsequent run in the same period hits the empty branch, so the advertised one-click flow silently fails after the first use. Repro: POST /api/payouts/run-now twice with Bearer test_session_supertoken, then GET /api/payouts - only one persisted batch exists. Mitigation: return {"batch_id": None, ...} on the empty path and guard the two frontend call sites on batch_id/total_amount.
